newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Morgan to face constituents at meetings.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Morgan to face constituents at meetings.

text.p: Embattled New Zealand First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan has called a series of hui (meetings) in his Te Tai Hauauru electorate over his involvement in Maori language broadcaster Aotearoa Television Network (ATN).
Meanwhile Deputy Prime Minister and New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Monday refused to answer when asked if he ruled out Morgan resigning over the ATN issue.
"I want you to tell me why you rule it in?" he asked Reuters.
Opposition MPs have called for Morgan to resign after revelations he spent $4,000 of ATN money on expensive clothes. They have hinted they will expose more details when the House resumes on Tuesday.
The Serious Fraud Office and the Registrar of Companies have launched separate inquiries into the financial affairs of ATN.
Morgan claimed he had the authority to spend the money, including $89 on a pair of underpants, although senior staff at the station have denied this.
The meetings in Morgan's electorate would start on Friday, but Morgan is due to brief the New Zealand First caucus on his involvement on Tuesday.
"I want to be face to face with the 11,000 people who put me into parliament as their representative to talk with them about issues they've only heard through the media," Morgan said.

In his statement he rejected claims that he snubbed Maori Queen Dame Te Atairangikaahu by not attending a weekend meeting. He said he had had several long-standing electorate meetings which had precedence over the poukai.
Peters said the meeting at the weekend was not the appropriate forum for a test of one individual at the expense of the Maori Queen's interests.
The National-New Zealand First coalition government holds 61 seats in the 120 seat parliament, but would be unlikely to fall if Morgan resigned.

Two centre-right parties with a total of nine MPs which are not part of the coalition would be likely to support continued centre-right government, although it might prove diffficult to win support for the full government programme, hammered out after October's election.
